storyContext.problem: Feature 1 shipped a headless HTTP API. Employees and admins need a browser interface to consume the same endpoints without touching the backend. This story delivers an Angular 21 SPA covering the six backend surfaces on main, by adopting an existing spike and closing its gaps.

baseline.decision: Framework is Angular 21, not React + Vite. The instructor spike on spike/story-2-1-angular is adopted as Feature 2's deliverable.
baseline.path: frontend-angular/ - NOT frontend/. The spike deliberately left frontend/ free.

It branched before story 1.8 landed, so its diff against main DELETES backend code and tests (GlobalExceptionHandler -26, MenuControllerTest -26, OrderControllerTest -57). policy.rule: Frontend is decoupled: no changes to pom.xml, Java sources, or application.yml.
State is Angular signals, computed() for derived values. No NgRx, no third-party store, no RxJS subjects for view state.
httpResource for reads, HttpClient on LunchApi for mutations (spine AD-11). After a successful mutation call reload() - never patch a local copy of server state. No Axios, no fetch wrappers.
Angular Router, exactly three lazily-loaded routes (/, /orders, /admin) plus ** redirect to /.
Component-scoped CSS, already in place. Do not add Tailwind or a component library on top. Do not mix styling systems.
AC 2.1.10 (design) executes before any component change.
X-Admin: true is attached by the interceptor ONLY when the router is under /admin, derived from the active route and never from stored state (spine AD-10). No component sets identity headers itself.
X-User-Id is held in a signal, sourced from a "Sign in as" input, persisted to localStorage with try/catch on every access so private-browsing degrades to a non-persistent session.
One apiErrorMessage() helper is the only place an HttpErrorResponse becomes display text. Renders ApiError.message, never .code. No non-2xx is silently swallowed (spine AD-12).

DONE. The design step ran 2026-09-03 via bmad-ux and produced TWO peer spines, both status:final with no open questions: frontend-angular/DESIGN.md (visual identity, light AND dark tokens) and frontend-angular/EXPERIENCE.md (IA, nine states, behaviour, accessibility floor, three flows). BOTH SPINES ARE THE ACCEPTANCE BAR for every visual and behavioural AC and win over any mock or restyle. The original spike DESIGN.md is preserved verbatim as SPIKE-FINDINGS.md.

Theme follows prefers-color-scheme only. Redefine the SAME custom properties inside the media query; components must NEVER branch on theme. No in-app toggle, no persisted preference, no mention of theme in the UI. Only possible if rule P16 holds.
Every colour, border and radius resolves through var(--token). No component hard-codes a hex. A hard-coded hex looks correct in light and breaks in dark, which is why AC 2.1.14 gates AC 2.1.15.

Destructive actions are two-step and INLINE ON THE ROW - never a modal. There are no dialog components in this application: a modal would drag in a focus trap, escape handling, scroll locking, a backdrop and rounded-corner elevation that DESIGN.md rules out. Exactly one row armed at a time; Escape and Keep both disarm; the safe option is the default.

Every form field carries aria-invalid bound to touched-and-invalid plus aria-describedby pointing at its own message element, which reserves height so validation never shifts layout. The /admin route already complies and is the reference; the order form does not and must be brought in line.

Port 5173 is load-bearing. npm start stays pinned to `ng serve --port 5173` because WebConfig allows exactly one CORS origin. Do not add a dev-server proxy - it was deliberately rejected so the existing CORS config stays exercised (spine AD-13).
The server owns ordering (spine AD-18). Clients render the response order as received.
Standalone components, OnPush, inject() over constructor injection, input() over @Input(), native @if/@for, selector prefix lunch-.

The reactive-forms (/) vs signal-forms (/admin) split is deliberate, was the spike's experiment, and unifying it is OUT OF SCOPE. Note it in the PR so a reviewer does not read it as sloppiness. Signal forms cost 34 kB raw on the /admin lazy chunk for a two-field form.

criterion.reason: violated by the baseline's restyle commit

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Menu view (/) lists today's menu from GET /api/v1/menu; each item shows name and priceChf formatted as CHF AND NOTHING ELSE. NO availability indicator: the endpoint returns available items only (spine AD-6), so such an indicator would always read "available". Do not build UI for a state the API cannot return. VIOLATED BY THE BASELINE: commit 6aadae6 ("restyle the menu route with the frontend-design skill") added <span class="flag" [class.flag-out]="!item.available"> rendering 'available'/'unavailable'. None of the four preceding spike commits contain it - the polish pass introduced it disguised as styling. The .flag-out branch is unreachable and its CSS is dead. REQUIRED: remove the .flag span from menu-page.html and the .flag/.flag-out rules from menu-page.css; KEEP the dotted .leader (load-bearing to the editorial aesthetic, not an availability cue); extend menu-page.spec.ts to assert the row contains name and price only, so a future restyle cannot reintroduce it silently. ALSO ADD THE MISSING EMPTY STATE (the / route is the one surface lacking one): "No dishes on the menu today."

criterion.reason: implemented but untested; per-field errors owed

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Order form (on /) picks menu item + quantity (1-10), submits via POST /api/v1/orders with X-User-Id. Not ticked until AC 2.1.12 covers it. ADDITIONALLY REQUIRED - per-field error association (policy P18): the order form currently surfaces validation only through the shared banner with no field-level association. The /admin route already does it properly and its pattern is now the standard - aria-invalid bound to touched-and-invalid, aria-describedby pointing at its own message element, message element reserving min-height so validation does not shift layout. Apply to both fields.

My orders view (/orders) lists the caller's orders from GET /api/v1/orders/me showing item name, quantity, status, and a Cancel button next to each SUBMITTED order. The baseline resolves names from GET /api/v1/menu (available items only) and falls back to a truncated id, so an order for a since-unavailable item shows no name. REQUIRED: resolve via GET /api/v1/menu/{id} (story 2.7; the only availability-bypassing read, spine AD-7), one request per DISTINCT menuItemId, cached per id, so N orders over M distinct items cost M requests not N. Verify with MenuSeedData's seeded available=false item - the only runtime fixture that exercises this path.

Cancel action, now TWO-STEP. The single-click cancel (PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel, reload(), confirmation on success) is implemented and untested; a confirm step is now required, which reopens this AC. INLINE ON THE ROW, NOT A MODAL (policy P17): (1) cell shows Cancel; (2) one click ARMS the row - 3px solid var(--accent) left border, var(--accent-soft) ground, cell swaps to "Cancel order" plus "Keep", nothing sent yet; (3) focus moves to the confirm, Escape or Keep disarms, arming another row disarms this one, exactly one armed at a time; (4) confirming fires the PATCH, both buttons disable, confirm label becomes "Cancelling"; (5) success reloads and shows "Order cancelled.", failure shows the banner and disarms. TWO ACCESSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS SPECIFIC TO THIS PATTERN: the confirm button accessible name must identify the ROW not just the verb (aria-label="Cancel order of Risotto aux champignons") because "Cancel order" alone is ambiguous in a table and a screen-reader user tabbing in has no visual row context; and arming is announced through a POLITE live region, never role=alert, because arming is not an error.
Admin add-item view (/admin): form for name + priceChf, POSTs to /api/v1/menu/items with X-Admin: true.
Identity handling per policies P7 and P8. The adopted implementation EXCEEDS the original AC: deriving the admin header from the active route makes it true by construction. Keep it that way.
Error display renders ApiError.message (never .code) on non-2xx; never silently swallows a non-2xx response (policy P9).

Design captured as TWO peer spines in frontend-angular/: DESIGN.md (visual identity - nine ratified colour tokens, eight type roles, spacing, the radius:0 rule, per-component visual specs, Do's and Don'ts) and EXPERIENCE.md (information architecture, the eight-state vocabulary, component behaviour, interaction primitives, accessibility floor, three named-protagonist flows; cross-references DESIGN.md tokens by name). REWORDED 2026-09-03: this AC originally asked for wireframes in a single DESIGN.md. bmad-ux produces two peer contracts and, following the Google Labs design.md spec, its DESIGN.md means VISUAL IDENTITY while layout, states and behaviour belong to EXPERIENCE.md. The AC now names both rather than describing content that lives in the other file. Brownfield run - the visual identity already existed in the spike's CSS, so the spines RATIFY rather than invent. The spike's original DESIGN.md is preserved verbatim as SPIKE-FINDINGS.md (an engineering evaluation report recording two defects in Angular's own reference material). FIVE open [ASSUMPTION] tags remain in the spines for the participant or instructor: /'s empty-state copy, the light-only palette declaration, per-field error association on the order form, whether Cancel stays unguarded, and whether the three protagonists are replaced with real ones.

Remove the client-side re-sort. my-orders-page re-sorts with b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt) although findAllByUserIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc already returns newest-first. The server owns ordering (spine AD-18); the second mechanism agrees today only because Jackson emits fixed-width UTC ISO-8601 and drifts silently if that changes. Delete the sort; render the response order as received. The view must still display newest-first - assert against an already-sorted mocked response.
Close the test gaps. Add my-orders-page.spec.ts and extend coverage so all three routes have tests. Six minimum cases enumerated in testScaffolding.

Add a real linter: `ng add @angular-eslint/schematics` plus a `lint` script. npm run lint must pass on all committed frontend-angular/ code with no rules disabled. THIS STORY EXPLICITLY AUTHORISES the new dev dependencies - the Angular 21 scaffold ships Prettier but no ESLint and package.json has no lint script, so the DoD's lint gate was previously unsatisfiable. CLAUDE.md's no-new-dependencies rule targets pom.xml; this is a separate manifest. Keep Prettier green alongside.

Every colour, border and radius resolves through a token; no component hard-codes a hex. AUDIT - var(--token) vs hard-coded hex per file: app.css 14/0 OK, menu-page.css 25/0 OK, my-orders-page.css 0/2 FAIL, admin-page.css 0/2 FAIL, error-banner inline styles 0/3 FAIL. Only the shell and / were ever restyled. FOUR off-palette values to DELETE rather than tokenise - the palette already covers each: #a4262c (error ink, ErrorBanner + admin-page.css) becomes var(--accent) #b1341c; #fdf3f4 (error ground, ErrorBanner) becomes var(--accent-soft) #f0d9c8; #107c10 (confirmation, my-orders-page.css + admin-page.css) becomes var(--ok) #2f6b3d; #e5e5e5 (table rule, my-orders-page.css) becomes var(--rule) #ddd6c8. ALSO: drop ErrorBanner's border-radius:4px (DESIGN.md Shapes - radius is 0 everywhere), and unify .confirmation on the menu-page treatment (3px solid var(--ok) left border plus var(--ok) text) so the same component stops having two appearances depending on route.

Dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. Nine dark tokens are specified in DESIGN.md Colors. Redefine the SAME custom properties inside the dark media query; components must not branch on theme (policy P15). ONLY POSSIBLE ONCE AC 2.1.14 LANDS - a hard-coded hex looks fine in light and breaks in dark, which is why the two are paired. NOT A PLAIN INVERSION: the dark ground is a warm brown-black #1c1714, not neutral grey and not #000, so the paper metaphor survives as unlit paper; paper-deep stays DARKER than the sheet, preserving the tonal relationship; the accent LIFTS to #e8674a because #b1341c on #1c1714 fails AA. TWO THINGS CHANGE BEYOND COLOUR: the canvas grain lightens instead of darkening (rgba(240,235,225,0.02)), and the sheet drop shadow is DROPPED ENTIRELY - against a dark ground it reads as a black smear, so depth comes from the tonal step alone. NO IN-APP TOGGLE - system preference is the whole mechanism. WARNING: the dark contrast ratios in DESIGN.md are COMPUTED, NOT MEASURED. Verify each pair with a contrast checker before ticking. accent-dark on accent-soft-dark is tightest at roughly 4.5:1 - if it measures below, lighten accent-dark rather than darkening the ground, which would break the error banner border.

knownTraps.trap: httpResource needs an explicit detectChanges() to fire its request. Awaiting whenStable() first deadlocks against a request nothing has answered yet.

trap.source: angular-developer skill, testing-fundamentals.md - states the OPPOSITE

knownTraps.trap: After flush(), an async submit callback's continuation runs in a later microtask, so whenStable() settles BEFORE the signals are written. Yield explicitly.
The reference shows a service annotated @Service(). Angular has no @Service decorator - it is @Injectable(). Copied verbatim it will not compile.

The CLI's generated CLAUDE.md says "Prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones" and never mentions signal forms, contradicting angular-developer/SKILL.md which prefers signal forms on v21+.
